items.title: 93% of real bets have blank 'category' even though Kalshi has the data
items.action: Found 2026-08-25 while adding a win-rate-by-category chart to the dashboard at the owner's request -- only 4 of 51 rows in signals.csv have a populated `category` (Sports, Economics, Entertainment, Climate and Weather); the rest are blank. Confirmed this is NOT a Kalshi data-completeness limitation: live-queried one of the blank rows directly (KXAPRPOTUS-26AUG21-39.2, logged 2026-08-20 with category blank) via the exact core.kalshi.fetch_event_detail() call this codebase already uses, and Kalshi returned category='Politics' with no error. A separate live check of core.kalshi.fetch_events() (the bulk /events listing main.py's Step 2 primarily uses) showed 400/400 currently-open events have a non-empty category field. The data exists on Kalshi's side; something in Leviathan's own capture path is dropping it for most real bets. Two concrete, verified gaps that plausibly explain this (not necessarily the only ones -- not fully root-caused to a single cause): (1) main.py's fallback path (kalshi.fetch_markets(), used only when kalshi.fetch_events() itself raises) attaches no category at all -- confirmed by reading the code, this path has zero category-attachment logic. (2) kalshi.fetch_near_dated_markets()'s per-event category backfill (core/kalshi.py ~L364-371) wraps each fetch_event_detail() call in a bare 'except Exception: event_meta[et] = ("", "")' with no logging at all -- unlike the sibling events-catalog loop in main.py, which does print a warning on a similar failure. Any transient failure (rate limit, timeout) here silently produces a permanently blank category with no trace in the logs. Also worth checking once picked up: main.py's events-catalog loop only fetches kalshi.fetch_events()'s top max_events (default 100, config.markets.max_events) events by recent activity -- a market whose parent event falls outside that window at fetch time would never get matched to a category-bearing event object at all. Needs: add logging to the silent except block in fetch_near_dated_markets so failures are at least visible, then watch the next several real-run logs to see which of these paths (or something else) is actually the dominant cause before writing a fix. Cannot backfill most existing blank rows -- Kalshi's API returns 404/not_found for expired events (confirmed live on KXCABLEAVE-26MAY22-26SEP, a 2026-07 signal), so the historical gap is permanent; this is about stopping new bets from landing blank going forward.
items.notes:
Dashboard side handled separately, same day: the category chart shows 'Uncategorized' as an honestly-labeled bucket with a caption explaining it's a known, tracked pipeline gap rather than lost or hidden data, per the same day's plain-language accessibility pass.

RESOLVED 2026-08-26: fixed both concrete gaps rather than waiting to observe live logs to pick one -- fixing both makes the dominant-cause question moot. (1) Extracted the per-event category/series_ticker backfill (event_ticker dedup + fetch_event_detail loop) out of fetch_near_dated_markets() into a new shared core.kalshi.attach_event_category_metadata() helper, and wired it into main.py's fetch_markets() fallback path (previously zero category-attachment logic there). (2) The silent 'except Exception: event_meta[et] = ("", "")' in that helper now prints a [warn] line with the event_ticker and error before defaulting, matching the sibling events-catalog loop's pattern -- future transient failures will show up in run logs instead of vanishing. Added test_attach_event_category_metadata_prints_warning_on_failure and test_attach_event_category_metadata_one_call_per_unique_event to tests/test_kalshi_near_dated.py; existing fetch_near_dated_markets tests re-verified unaffected by the extraction. Full suite green (2270 passed, 1 skipped). NOT fixed: main.py's events-catalog loop still only fetches the top max_events (config.markets.max_events, default 100) events by recent activity, so a market whose parent event falls outside that window still won't match a category-bearing event object -- this is a real, separate, lower-confidence gap (not verified live to actually be occurring) and would need its own investigation if categories are still landing blank after this fix. Historical blank rows remain unbackfillable (Kalshi 404s on expired events) -- unchanged, this was never in scope.

items.action: Split out 2026-08-26 from smart-money-fills-table-missing (which only fixed the silent-failure visibility problem, not the underlying gap). Deliberately priority 4, not urgent -- a real feature build, not a quick fix, and the downstream items it feeds are all still far from their own threshold regardless.

BUILT 2026-09-07 (user go-ahead: "tackle the ready items that are good to go if not gated"). Schema added to core/logger.py's _init_db() -- smart_money_fills(id, wallet, trader_name, poly_slug, outcome, poly_title, kalshi_ticker, entry_price, position_val, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, resolved, hit, resolved_pct_pnl, resolved_cash_pnl, resolved_at), UNIQUE(wallet, poly_slug, outcome). kalshi_ticker is a schema placeholder, not yet populated -- the raw position dicts fetch_watchlist_positions works with don't carry the cross-referenced Kalshi ticker (that mapping only exists later, in run_smart_money_scan's separate all_signals list); wiring that through is a small, real follow-up, not done here to keep this build scoped to the core ask.

backlog/checker.py needed NO changes -- its resolved_count_per_wallet_max query already targeted this exact table/schema shape (written defensively in anticipation, 2026-08-26) and its _data_gaps mechanism already distinguished 'table missing' from 'genuinely zero'; creating the table was the only missing piece. Live-verified: the 'not tracked yet -- smart_money_fills table missing' caveat is now gone from checker output, correctly reporting a real 0 (table exists, empty) instead of an unknown-data-gap state.

14 new tests in tests/test_smart_money_fills.py (insert/refresh/skip-unverified/skip-missing-slug for the writer; hit/miss/never-infer-from-absence/ignores-still-open/skip-unverified for backfill; empty/ignores-unresolved/real-max-across-wallets for the reader). items.title: DailyRun missed its 2026-08-30 run silently -- fixed 3 real gaps that let it happen unnoticed
items.action: Found 2026-08-30: main.py's scheduled 7am run launched a real process (confirmed via Task Scheduler operational event log, PID 20048, ran 21m58s) and Task Scheduler reported clean exit 0, but zero rows appeared in the `runs` table and no field-report email arrived. Only reason anyone found out: heartbeat_check.py's own 30h-staleness alert fired 19 hours later. Root-caused to three compounding gaps: (1) main.py's Step 1 Kalshi-auth-failure path (`except Exception: print(...); return`) was completely silent -- no alert email, unlike the sibling shape-anomaly abort path a few lines below it which does send one. The ~22-minute runtime is consistent with kalshi-sdk's own documented exponential-backoff retry exhausting itself on a transient failure before finally raising. Kalshi auth confirmed working normally again same day (not an ongoing outage). (2) scripts/schedule_setup.ps1's Task Scheduler action launched python directly with zero output capture -- unlike every other Leviathan-* task, which redirects via a cmd.exe wrapper (documented elsewhere as a fix for a known Task-Scheduler-specific hang with unredirected output, not just a diagnostics nicety). The actual error message from today's failure is unrecoverable. (3) Even with redirection, Python fully buffers stdout once piped to a file -- confirmed live via a manual trigger that was force-stopped (Stop-ScheduledTask) and left a 0-byte log despite several steps' worth of prior output, meaning ExecutionTimeLimit or any other forced kill would have silently lost everything printed up to that point too.
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-30, same day. (1) main.py: the auth-failure return now sends an alert email (subject 'Leviathan ALERT — Kalshi auth failed, run aborted'), matching the shape-anomaly path's pattern exactly. Verified live via a mocked kalshi.authenticate() failure -- confirmed the correct subject/body and exactly one send_report call. Untestable via the normal pytest suite (main.py's orchestration has no test harness by design, same as every other main() code path -- verified by direct invocation instead, consistent with tests/test_market_shape_validation.py's own documented precedent). (2) schedule_setup.ps1: switched the Action to the same cmd.exe + `>> logfile 2>&1` wrapper every other setup_*.ps1 already uses, moved $LogFile from an unused repo-root path (not even gitignored) to logs/leviathan_scheduler.log (matching every other script's log location and staying covered by .gitignore's logs/ rule). Re-registered live, confirmed the new Action definition via Get-ScheduledTask readback, confirmed LogonType/battery/restart settings from the two prior 2026-08-27 fixes all survived the re-registration. (3) Added `-u` (unbuffered) to the python invocation -- verified live with an isolated smoke test (a throwaway script + Start-Process + immediate read) that output actually appears in the log file progressively, not just on clean exit. Caught and immediately corrected one of my own mistakes mid-fix: a live Task-Scheduler smoke trigger of DailyRun collided with an already-running catch-up main.py invocation from the same session -- stopped the redundant one within seconds via Stop-ScheduledTask once noticed, no duplicate signals were logged (confirmed after the fact). Did NOT touch weekly_code_audit.py's OWN separate exit-code-trust bug found in the same investigation -- see resolved-count-per-category-max-wrong-column's sibling item weekly-code-audit-exit-code-not-proof-of-report for that fix.

items.title: Windows Defender (MsMpEng.exe) + Docker Desktop likely causing real slowdowns/instability on this machine
items.action: Found 2026-08-30 while investigating a garbled weekly_code_audit.py run and a main.py catch-up run that appeared stuck on one step for a long stretch (both eventually completed -- confirmed slow, not truly deadlocked). Live process check: MsMpEng.exe (Windows Defender's real-time scanning engine) at ~206,949 CPU-seconds (~57.5 cumulative hours), com.docker.backend also consuming real CPU/memory in the background. Even lightweight, normally-instant tool calls (a repo-wide grep, ripgrep) took 20-120+ seconds or had to be backgrounded during this window. items.notes:

A common, standard mitigation worth considering: add a Windows Defender exclusion for the Leviathan project directory (and/or the python.exe / claude CLI executables) to stop real-time scanning from re-scanning this project's own heavy, repeated file I/O. Also worth considering: whether Docker Desktop needs to run continuously on this machine, or only when actually needed. No code action possible on this item from within the repo.

CHECK-IN 2026-09-03: MsMpEng.exe currently shows ~0 accumulated CPU time (a fresh process instance, not proof the underlying contention risk is gone) and com.docker.backend is at ~9.1 CPU-hours across two processes -- lower apparent pressure than 8/30's snapshot, and no repeat of the slow-tool-call symptom observed today. FIXED 2026-09-08 (explicit user go-ahead): added a Windows Defender real-time-scan exclusion for the Leviathan project folder (`Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath 'C:\Users\Administrator\Downloads\Leviathan'`), verified live via `Get-MpPreference`. items.title: Bounded Trial: Stronger Model for Main Scoring Pass
items.action: Using the now-live config.llm.cli_model_override (see wire-llm-model-cli-flag, done -- no depends_on here since that item is already done as of this item's own creation, not a real gate), run a bounded 5-7 scheduled-run trial with a stronger model (e.g. 'opus') for main.py's Claude-scored pipeline only. Compare signal counts/pass-rates/edge distributions against the preceding baseline window, then revert the single config key back to null.

Deliberately NOT executed as part of the wiring fix -- this is a separate, later go/no-go decision, not a default change. Real trade-off, live-verified 2026-08-31: a heavier model is slower per call and consumes more of the flat-rate Pro-plan usage/session budget, which could REDUCE how many markets are scorable per day -- directly cutting against the 'collect data faster' half of the original request even if per-call scoring quality improves. Direction of the quality effect (more genuine signals clearing thresholds vs. becoming more conservative and passing fewer) is unproven without this controlled test. If run: main.py's model_used report field currently sources from the separate, cosmetic scoring.scorer_model config key -- keep it manually in sync with whatever cli_model_override actually was for that run's window, or results will be misattributed to the wrong model in reporting. Recommending to the user: revert llm.cli_model_override to null now rather than spend 2 more scheduled runs chasing a narrower confidence interval on a comparison that already shows no clear benefit -- flagged to the user directly rather than reverted unilaterally, since changing the live scoring model is a real production behavior/cost change, not a safe-default judgment call.

REVERTED 2026-09-05, user-authorized in chat ("yes revert the opus trial"). config.json's llm.cli_model_override set back to null. items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-31. Since core/kalshi.py unconditionally imports the kalshi-sdk package (not installed in the dashboard's actual Python environment -- streamlit isn't in the project's own venv either), the tiny confirmed kalshi_market_url() URL-format logic is deliberately duplicated inline in the dashboard page rather than imported, avoiding a real import crash. 2 new logger tests, 3 new accounts tests, full suite green (2309 passed). (2) dashboard/pages/2_Signal_Breakdown.py -- a stale hardcoded "13/46" resolved-count figure in the CLV-drift empty-state message, now computed live from the current signals DataFrame instead. (3) dashboard/pages/3_Signal_Log.py -- same wallet/identity-conflation pattern as the whale-streak fix, in the whale_detected KPI help text ("a big bettor... someone with information is confident") -- reworded to state plainly there is no identity behind the signal. items.action: User feedback: dashboard/live category diversity felt low. The 4 categories missing from signals.category (Social, Health, World, Transportation) are just thin market slices (19/10/7/1 open markets respectively) that haven't produced a flagged signal yet, not a code gap -- no fix needed or possible there short of waiting for real signal volume.

items.title: Require genuine search effort before PASS, without lowering the evidence bar
items.action: User request: "I don't want to pass on bets... do additional research or find insight that favors a yes or no decision." This conflated two different asks that needed separating before building anything -- flagged to the user first rather than building either silently. (1) 'Research harder before concluding PASS' is legitimate and safe. (2) 'Never pass, always call a side' would corrupt the exact track record this project uses to measure whether real skill exists -- core/sizing.py's own docstring already documents a real precedent for this failure mode (edge-magnitude sizing made hypothetical P&L ~4x WORSE on real data, because confidence and correctness weren't the same thing at low sample size). Forcing a directional call where the model currently sees no edge is the same mechanism at the decision layer instead of the sizing layer. User confirmed they wanted only the research-depth version. Investigated the actual scoring prompt (core/scorer.py's SYSTEM_PROMPT, 47 numbered calibration rules) before touching anything: nearly every rule already says 'default to PASS unless [narrow, well-reasoned condition]' -- this is not a system passing lazily, it's one deliberately engineered against over-interpreting weak announcement-type evidence (Rule 3: 'announced != completed', applied across IPOs, product releases, M&A, tax legislation, etc). The actual gap: the prompt's ONLY instruction about search behavior itself was one generic sentence ('Use web search to find relevant recent information') with zero diligence requirement before applying any of the 47 PASS-default rules -- meaning a model that searched once, found nothing, and defaulted to PASS was indistinguishable from one that searched thoroughly and found nothing. Confirmed whale/smart-money/Polymarket cross-market data is already surfaced in the per-market prompt block when present (core.scorer.build_prompt reads m.get('whale_data')/m.get('smart_money')/m.get('poly')) -- not a hidden-data gap, already wired.
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-01. Added a 'RESEARCH DILIGENCE' paragraph to SYSTEM_PROMPT, positioned before Rule 1 (applies to every rule, not appended as an afterthought): requires at least 2-3 distinct searches (recent news with an alternate phrasing if the first search misses, the specific entity's current status, explicit engagement with any CROSS-MARKET/POLYMARKET/SMART MONEY data already in the prompt) before concluding PASS. Explicitly states it does NOT lower the evidence bar the numbered rules set -- a thorough search that genuinely finds nothing still validly results in PASS; only an under-researched PASS no longer qualifies. Deliberately did NOT touch the evidence-interpretation rules themselves, the edge_threshold, or the PASS branch's decision logic -- this only strengthens the research step that happens before those rules get applied. No new subprocess/CLI-call overhead: --allowedTools WebSearch already permits multiple searches within the existing single scoring call, this only instructs the model to actually use that budget. 2 new tests (test_system_prompt_has_research_diligence_instruction, test_research_diligence_precedes_calibration_rules) in tests/test_scorer.py, all 179 existing scorer/blind_scorer tests unaffected. Full suite verification pending at commit time. Effect on signals_generated is unmeasured and won't be knowable until real scheduled runs accumulate under the new prompt -- not something to check via a manual trigger, per the same reasoning as the Opus trial (avoid competing for Pro/CLI usage with the concurrent replay-corpus build).

items.title: Capture real token/cache usage from the live CLI backend instead of hardcoded 0
items.action: User asked to research reducing Leviathan's own token footprint (after a separate detour into whether OmniRoute could help -- rejected, since routing Claude Code through it means replacing native Pro/Max OAuth with an OmniRoute-issued token, which needs OmniRoute to hold its own working session against the user's Anthropic account -- real credential handling outside what should be done autonomously, and it directly fights an existing deliberate safeguard in this codebase: _score_via_cli() strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the subprocess env specifically to force native Pro-plan auth). Investigated the live CLI backend's actual token behavior empirically rather than guessing: two consecutive `claude --print --output-format json` calls with the identical ~42KB SYSTEM_PROMPT showed real Anthropic prompt caching already working across separate subprocess invocations, using a 1-hour TTL (not the usual 5-minute default) -- cache_creation_input_tokens on call 1, a much larger cache_read_input_tokens and roughly half the cost on call 2. Since Leviathan's several Claude calls per run (one batch score_markets() + one rescore_single_market()/ground_citations() call per shortlisted pick) all share the same system prompt and happen within minutes of each other, this caching most likely already applies today. The real, concrete gap found: the live CLI call used --output-format text, which discards all usage telemetry -- this is why runs.tokens_used/cost_usd have been hardcoded to 0 for every single CLI-backend run, always, with zero visibility into real cache-hit rates or footprint. Deliberately did NOT trim the 47-rule system prompt itself to save cache-creation cost -- that's real, carefully-tuned calibration content, and judging what's 'rarely used enough to cut' needs actual usage-frequency data, which this fix is the prerequisite for, not a guess to make now.
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-02. Switched core.scorer._score_via_cli()'s --output-format from text to json, parsed the resulting envelope ({'result', 'usage', 'total_cost_usd', ...}) for the actual model text (same fence/bracket extraction as before, just applied to envelope['result'] instead of raw stdout) plus real input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_creation_input_tokens/cache_read_input_tokens/cost_usd, matching core.llm.score_via_api's existing token_info shape exactly. items.title: fetch_events() recency window structurally excludes newly-listed, thin markets
items.action: core.kalshi.fetch_events() caps at config.markets.max_events (400) events, sorted by last_updated_ts desc ('recently active events first'). Live-verified 2026-09-04: NFL's 2026 season and college football's are both underway (user prompted this check -- 64 open KXNFLGAME markets, 500 open KXNCAAFGAME markets, oldest created 2026-08-25), but ZERO NFL or NCAAF game events appear anywhere in a live fetch_events() call's top 400 -- confirmed both by directly inspecting that call's real output and by querying the signals table (0 KXNFLGAME/KXNCAAFGAME rows ever logged, all-time). Root cause: thin, newly-listed markets (liquidity_dollars=0.00 on several sampled) don't generate frequent price updates, so their last_updated_ts stays stale while high-churn categories (economics rate ladders, politics) constantly refresh and permanently occupy the top 400 slots. This isn't football-specific -- it's a structural blind spot for ANY new, thin-volume market family in its first days/weeks, which is exactly when a mispricing would be most likely to still exist before the crowd corrects it. The daily pipeline has been running normally (LastTaskResult=0) this whole time with no visible error, since nothing about this is a failure -- it's precisely bounded to do exactly this.
items.notes:
FIXED 2026-09-04 -- not in fetch_events() itself (raising max_events was ruled out: live pagination showed the first NFL/NCAAF event at raw position 3400 of 6000, so a workable max_events bump would be enormous and still not general). Fixed in core.kalshi.fetch_near_dated_markets(), the existing purpose-built near-dated supplement (already merged into all_markets in both main.py and analysis/snapshot_markets.py) -- it turned out to have the identical 'recency crowds out newness' bug at a different layer, which is why testing it live also returned 0 football despite football closing well inside its 14-day window.
Root cause, live-verified: the day-by-day close-date chunking walked days 0..13 but (1) the outer loop stopped entirely once the GLOBAL target_count was hit, and low-flood early days (day 0: 199 real markets from a single page) exhausted it before the walk ever reached day 9-10 where football closes, and (2) even with that removed, the final list was truncated in day order (collected[:target_count]), so day-9/10 markets were discarded anyway once days 0-1 alone exceeded target_count. Confirmed via live day-by-day breakdown (2026-09-04): KXNFLGAME/KXNCAAFGAME markets first appear on day 9 (55 markets) and day 10 (166 markets) of a live 14-day scan, and have 0% overlap with a live fetch_events() call's output -- i.e. no other code path ever surfaced them either.
Fix: each day is capped at a fair per-day quota (target_count // max_days, min 1) of 'guaranteed' picks, and the day-loop always walks every day up to max_days (bounded only by the pre-existing max_pages hard cost cap) instead of stopping once the global target is hit. Anything a day collects beyond its own quota is kept as 'surplus' (already fetched over the wire at zero extra cost, since a single page returns far more than most days' quota) and used to backfill the final list up to target_count if guaranteed picks alone don't fill it -- so abundant days don't lose total yield, they just no longer get to crowd out thin/late days. Live-measured against the real 2026-09-04 API: same page count (38, under the existing 40-page config cap, no config change needed) and same final count (300) as the old code's typical yield, but now includes 6 KXNFLGAME/KXNCAAFGAME markets and 37 total NFL/NCAAF-family markets where there were previously zero in any live run.
Generalizes beyond football per the original diagnosis -- any market family whose close dates land after an early abundant day was structurally unreachable before this fix, regardless of category.
core/kalshi.py: fetch_near_dated_markets() rewritten (per-day quota + guaranteed/surplus split), docstring extended with the root-cause and fix writeup. tests/test_kalshi_near_dated.py: all 14 existing tests pass unmodified (none of the existing fixtures exercise a case where the per-day cap binds tightly enough to change behavior -- verified by hand before implementing, not just after); 2 new tests added (test_per_day_quota_prevents_early_abundant_day_from_starving_later_day, test_leftover_budget_backfilled_from_abundant_day_surplus) directly reproducing the crowding bug and the no-regression backfill guarantee. Full suite green (2377 passed, 1 skipped).

items.title: Generic ' win ' heuristic catch-all misapplies its many-way rate to real 2-team games
items.action: win-catchall-recalibration (done, 2026-08-01) correctly dropped the generic ' win ' heuristic from 0.52 to the measured 0.08, explicitly declining to split the pattern by entrant count 'since that wasn't what was asked.' Live-verified 2026-09-04: that population never included a single NFL/NCAAF head-to-head game market -- confirmed via settled_markets, 0 KXNFLGAME/KXNCAAFGAME rows anywhere in the 12,600-row historical corpus that produced the 0.08 figure. Running the live scanner against the real, currently-open KXNCAAFGAME slate (bypassing the separate fetch_events() blind spot above via a direct series_ticker fetch) shows 17 of 500 open markets flagged HEURISTIC, every single one with base_rate=0.08 and label 'competition win' regardless of matchup (e.g. Ohio St. vs Texas, LSU vs Ole Miss) -- an 8% prior is defensible for a many-way tournament/award field, not a fair single-game moneyline between two real teams, where ~50% (or a real point-spread-implied probability) is the correct naive prior. This produces a spurious 40-90pp 'edge' against the market price on markets where none likely exists -- exactly the kind of false signal that would reach Claude scoring flagged as high-conviction. Needs a new, more specific rule intercepting 2-way head-to-head GAME series (KXNFLGAME/KXNCAAFGAME and any structurally similar single-elimination-matchup tickers) before the generic catch-all, the same pattern already used for down-ballot-election's 2-way sub-population split. Not fixed here -- flagging with real evidence rather than guessing at a replacement rate; the right prior (bare 50%, or informed by each team's record/ranking) needs its own real analysis, not an autonomous guess.
items.notes:
FIXED 2026-09-04: core/scanner.py adds a pre-check (_is_two_way_matchup_phrasing) before the shared _HEURISTIC_RULES loop, requiring BOTH ' vs ' and ' win ' in the title. Reuses the already-existing, already-validated 'sports game' rate (0.52) rather than inventing a new number -- this is the same real-world category as the existing 'win the game'/'win on' rule just below it in the table, only missed because Kalshi's verbose title template puts team names between 'win the' and 'vs' so the literal 'win the game' keyword never matches.
Why AND, not a simple keyword addition: ' vs ' alone also matches 443 real historical 'announcer mention' prop titles ("What will the announcers say during Wings vs Fire...?") that never mention winning and are a completely different market type -- confirmed empirically against settled_markets, not assumed. The AND combination itself is verified safe: zero of 12,600 historical settled_markets titles contain both ' vs ' and ' win ' together, so this cannot silently reclassify anything that already resolved.
Live-verified against the real, currently-open KXNCAAFGAME slate: all 17 previously-misfiring markets now correctly show base_rate=0.52/label='sports game' instead of 0.08/'competition win' (0 remain broken). Total flagged markets in that slate dropped 87->84 (3 near-toss-up games no longer spuriously flag at all now that the prior is honest) -- the remaining 14 HEURISTIC flags are now a legitimate signal (a neutral 52% prior disagreeing with a genuinely lopsided real market, e.g. Notre Dame heavily favored over Rice), not a fabricated 40-90pp fake edge from a wrong base rate. Full-corpus diff against all 12,600 settled_markets rows: zero rows changed classification (measured before/after, not assumed).
4 new tests in tests/test_scanner.py: the fix itself, the AND-not-OR guard (announcer-mention titles must NOT be swept in), confirmation that Kalshi's newer terser 'Team Name wins' title format (no ' vs ') is untouched, plus the corpus-diff finding recorded in this note (not as a live-DB-dependent test, to keep the suite offline/portable per this file's existing convention). Full suite green (2375 passed, 1 skipped).

items.title: External research: scheduler reliability options and forecasting-calibration benchmarks
items.action:
PM-directed research pass 2026-09-05 (user asked to research repos/AI developments that could help this project's workflows). Two findings worth the user's own evaluation, neither actioned autonomously since both involve either a real cost-policy question or a real methodology-comparison effort:

1. SCHEDULER RELIABILITY: task-scheduler-manual-trigger-stuck-queued has been an unresolved, recurring, root-cause-unidentified Windows Task Scheduler trigger-delivery failure for weeks (intermittent late/missed triggers, most recently 9/2 and 9/3). Anthropic shipped two relevant capabilities in 2026 that move scheduling off this machine entirely: (a) Claude Code server-side 'scheduled tasks' (per public write-ups, live as of ~September 2026, 'no device required') -- billing model relative to the existing Pro/CLI subscription this project already uses for core/scorer.py's _score_via_cli() could NOT be confirmed from search results alone and needs the user's own direct check against current Claude Code docs/account before any adoption decision, given the standing no-metered-API-spend policy; (b) Claude Managed Agents 'scheduled deployments' (Deployments API, cron-based, public beta since June 2026, 'no scheduler for you to build or host') -- this one IS confirmed metered/enterprise-plan (requires Claude for Work or an enterprise plan, billed via the Claude API, not the flat-rate CLI subscription), so it directly conflicts with the standing no-metered-spend policy unless the user wants to reconsider that boundary specifically for infra reliability. Neither was adopted or trialed here -- flagging both because the underlying problem (this machine's local Task Scheduler) has resisted every autonomous fix attempt so far and an external, Anthropic-hosted scheduler is architecturally the most direct fix, not because the cost tradeoff has been resolved.

2. EXTERNAL FORECASTING BENCHMARKS: found HINDCAST (arxiv 2607.14051, 'Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters') -- an academic paper tackling the same look-ahead-contamination and matched-time-baseline problem this project's own replay-instrument-validation/docs/METHODOLOGY.md already wrestles with; worth a read for possible refinements to how Leviathan's own replay corpus is built or validated. Also found several standardized LLM-forecasting benchmarks (ForecastBench, KalshiBench, Prophet Arena, Mirai) that score models against real resolved prediction-market questions with proper scoring rules (Brier) -- these could offer an external, apples-to-apples calibration check on the scorer that doesn't depend on this project's own small resolved-signal sample (n=33 as of 2026-09-05), which the just-closed edge-decay-analysis item shows is still too small/short-horizon-skewed to draw strong conclusions from on its own.
items.notes:
RESOLVED (finding 1 only) 2026-09-05, via a dedicated claude-code-guide agent citing current Claude Code docs directly (code.claude.com/docs/en/{costs,routines,desktop-scheduled-tasks}.md), not web-search speculation:
- Claude Code's own scheduled-task features DO run under the flat-rate Pro/Max subscription quota, same as interactive sessions -- 'Routines draw down subscription usage the same way interactive sessions do' (Costs doc). Confirmed distinct from Managed Agents (which stays confirmed-metered/enterprise, per the original finding).
- BUT there are two different scheduled-task mechanisms with different mechanics: 'cloud routines' (/schedule) run in an ephemeral Anthropic-hosted sandbox that clones the repo fresh each run -- NO access to local files, and critically NO access to this machine's local SQLite database (data/leviathan.db) or Windows-specific state. That rules cloud routines out as a Task Scheduler replacement outright, regardless of billing.
- 'Desktop scheduled tasks' (Claude Code Desktop app) are the one option that could actually work: runs ON this machine with full local file/DB access, subscription-only billing (not metered), 1-minute minimum interval (vs. cloud routines' 1 hour). The real tradeoff: it only fires while the Desktop app itself is running -- a different maintenance posture than a background Windows service (Task Scheduler runs headless; this would need the Desktop app kept open/running continuously on this machine).
- Not adopted or trialed here -- migrating the live daily pipeline's scheduling mechanism is an operational change with real risk if done hastily (this pipeline already has a live reliability problem; a rushed migration could make things worse before it makes them better), so this is presented as a recommendation for the user's decision, not something to switch over autonomously. If the user wants to pursue it: worth a bounded side-by-side trial (Desktop scheduled task running main.py alongside the existing Windows Task Scheduler entry, unchanged, for a week or two) before ever removing the existing entry.
Finding 2 (forecasting benchmarks) unchanged, still open.

FINDING 2 FOLLOW-UP 2026-09-07: KalshiBench (Nel, 2025) is the most directly relevant of the four -- its full dataset (1,531 questions, verified post-training outcomes, temporally filtered specifically to eliminate knowledge contamination) is public on HuggingFace at `2084Collective/kalshibench-v2`. This is a genuine off-the-shelf external validation corpus in this project's exact domain (real Kalshi questions, not a generic forecasting benchmark) -- more directly useful than reading the HINDCAST paper for methodology ideas, since it's an actual usable artifact rather than just a technique to borrow. Not pulled or integrated here -- that would mean downloading the dataset, mapping it onto Leviathan's schema, and running it through the scorer (architecturally similar to the existing backtesting.replay_runner corpus, real CLI-subscription cost not metered spend, but still a real new scoring-volume commitment) -- a deliberate scoped build worth its own go-ahead rather than folding into a research-findings pass. Recommendation: a bounded pilot (score ~50-100 sampled KalshiBench questions offline, compare Brier against the project's own live resolved-signal Brier) would give a real external calibration read independent of the project's own thin sample (n=37 as of 2026-09-07) -- worth prioritizing once there's appetite for it. Status left `ready` (not `done`) since this is a recommendation, not a completed build.

items.title: Audit remaining .get("ticker", "") call sites in core/report.py for the None-vs-missing crash pattern
items.action:
Found and fixed 2026-09-06 while removing the daily report's whale/smart-money sections (daily-report-drop-whale-smart-money): _week_whale_rows(), compile_weekly_digest()'s 'MARKETS FLAGGED THIS WEEK' table, and render_weekly_html()'s equivalent HTML row all crashed on a signal row with ticker=None, via the same class of bug as the 2026-08-05 whale_direction crash -- row.get('ticker', '') only substitutes the default for a MISSING key, not a present key whose value is explicitly None, and _trunc(None, ...) then raises TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len(). All three were fixed (row.get('ticker') or '' pattern) and caught by 2 new regression tests (test_week_whale_rows_none_ticker_and_title_do_not_crash and its sibling) that happened to exercise compile_weekly_digest/render_weekly_html end-to-end, not just the row-builder in isolation -- that's why 3 separate crash sites were found from one test.
NOT audited: 5 more .get('ticker', '') call sites remain in core/report.py (lines ~429, 945, 1081, 1412, 2014 as of this writing) that were not exercised by the specific test scenario used here. Each needs checking: (a) does the field feeding it ever come from a source where ticker could be an explicit None (vs. always a real string or truly missing key), and (b) does the value flow into a _trunc()/len()-style call that would crash on None, or just a dict key/comparison that would silently tolerate it. Scoped out of the current fix to avoid an unbounded audit while user-requested daily-report changes were pending -- worth a dedicated pass given how easily this exact bug class recurs (this is now the second real production crash from the identical pattern).
items.notes:
AUDITED 2026-09-07: checked all 5 remaining .get('ticker', '') sites (lines 429, 945, 1081, 1412, 2014) individually by tracing each into its actual downstream use. All 5 are genuinely safe -- either the value only ever reaches an f-string (None renders as the literal text 'None', cosmetic at worst, never a crash: lines 429, 945, 1412) or it's used purely as a dict key for deduplication/lookup (None works fine as a dict key in Python, no crash: lines 1081, 1970, 2014). None of the 5 originally-flagged sites needed a code change.

Broadening the check to the sibling field (title shares the identical crash mechanism via _wrap()/_trunc(), not just ticker) found ONE real, previously-unflagged crash: _signal_block()'s `title = s.get('title', '')` (line 430, immediately below the safe ticker line at 429) feeds directly into _wrap(), which calls textwrap.wrap() and raises TypeError on None the same way _trunc(None, ...) does. _signal_block() renders every NEW/REPEAT signal in the daily plain-text report (compile_report) -- a live crash path if any signal's title is ever explicitly None. Fixed with the same `s.get('title') or ''` pattern used everywhere else in this file, plus a new regression test (test_signal_block_none_title_does_not_crash). Full suite green throughout (2377 passed, 1 skipped).

Lesson for next time: the bug class is 'ticker OR title as an explicit-None value', not 'ticker specifically' -- a future audit of this pattern should grep both fields together from the start rather than treating a ticker-only audit as complete.

items.title: Entertainment award calibration check blocked by an apparent Emmy settlement-timing anomaly
items.action: The same systematic sweep that produced political-coup-couples-misfire / fda-adcom-broadcom-misfire / nasa-mission-hataoka-partial-fix also flagged "entertainment award" (grammy/oscar/academy award/emmy award/golden globe/tony award/bafta/sag/sundance, rate 0.20) as a candidate recalibration: n=236, predicted 20% vs actual 10.6%, a gap in the same range as sports-award's already-fixed +0.163. But decomposing the 236 real matches by which award show actually matched (event_ticker prefix) shows this is NOT a single homogeneous population the way sports-award/first-named-storm were. Tony Awards: 144 rows across 25 distinct real categories, exactly 1 YES per category (the actual winner among ~5-9 nominees) -- a clean, fully-resolved many-way field, actual rate 17.4%, only +0.026 off the current 0.20 (a gap this project has historically left alone -- comparable to first-named-storm's own +0.002 and hurricane-category-ladder's +0.05). Emmy Awards: 91 rows across 13 distinct categories, ZERO YES anywhere -- despite each category having its real, correct set of nominees (verified by sampling titles, e.g. KXEMMYLIMITEDACTO-26SEP14's 7 rows are the genuine 2026 Limited-Series-Actor nominees: Jamie Bell, David Harbour, Richard Gadd, etc.). This 0% is not trusted as a real signal: every one of the 91 rows has close_time AND settlement_ts of 2026-07-08, while the event_ticker's own suffix (26SEP14) encodes a September 14, 2026 ceremony date -- meaning Kalshi's data shows these fully resolved to NO more than two months before the actual televised ceremony this audit's own real-world date (2026-09-07) still precedes by a week. A binary "who won" market cannot honestly resolve before the event happens; either the true winner-determination row for each category is missing from settled_markets entirely (a coverage gap in backtesting/settled_fetcher.py, not a real population), or Kalshi structures these markets in some way this audit doesn't have visibility into without a live API call (out of scope for this pure-DB/SQL audit). Also found and quantified, but declined to fix: the bare keyword 'oscar' matches "Oscar Diaz" (a real Top Chef contestant's given name, 1 of 236 rows) -- the same substring-collision bug class as heuristic-substring-collision-sweep's three fixes, but here padding to ' oscar ' would NOT help (his name is a standalone word, not embedded in a longer one -- the same structurally-unfixable homograph shape as 'Nasa Hataoka' in the sibling item). Impact is negligible at this n (236) either way. Declining to change the 0.20 rate off the contaminated aggregate (10.6%), and declining to adopt the clean Tony-only number (17.4%) as a permanent replacement either -- a single award show's data shouldn't set the rate for the whole multi-show label without first understanding whether the Emmy anomaly is a settled_fetcher bug or a genuine Kalshi market-structure difference between the two shows. Flagging with the real evidence found rather than guessing, matching down-ballot-election-recalibration's precedent for a population too structurally uncertain to fix blind.
items.notes: No code change. Re-check after the real 2026-09-14 Emmy ceremony date has passed: if settled_markets picks up genuine post-ceremony Emmy winner rows at that point (a real YES appearing in an existing KXEMMY* event_ticker, or new ones), re-run analysis/heuristic_backtest.py and compare against this item's numbers to see whether the 0% Emmy rate was a timing artifact (winners simply hadn't been decided yet) or something else. Until then, treat 'entertainment award' as calibration-unverified due to a data anomaly, not as evidence supporting a 0.20 -> ~0.11 rate cut -- the clean Tony-only subset actually suggests the current rate is already close to right.

items.action: Found via a systematic sweep of core.scanner._HEURISTIC_RULES, not reactively -- every prior heuristic recalibration (win-catchall, sports-award, hurricane, down-ballot-election, win-catchall-two-team-game-misfire) was found because someone happened to notice a specific bug. This pass instead ran analysis/heuristic_backtest.py fresh against the full 12,600-row settled_markets corpus, then extracted every bare (unpadded, no internal space) keyword <=7 chars across all ~100 rules (55 candidates) and, for each, searched the full corpus for any OTHER real word containing it as a substring -- the exact mechanism this bug class needs. Bare 'coup' (political coup rule, rate 0.10) is a substring of 'Couples' -- confirmed against the full corpus: ALL 89 historical "political coup" matches (100%) traced to one ticker, KXLOVEISLANDUSARANK-26AUG31RTOP3 ("Will [Couple] finish in the Top 3 Couples in Love Island USA Season 8?"), zero real political-coup markets. A word-boundary regex check (\bcoup\b) across the same 12,600-row corpus found 0 genuine political-coup titles anywhere -- this heuristic has never once fired on real data. Fixed by padding the keyword to ' coup ' (same fix pattern already established elsewhere in this table: ' win ', ' dprk ', ' fired '), which structurally cannot match a substring embedded inside a longer word like 'Couples' while still matching genuine phrasing ("a coup in Venezuela"). Rate left unchanged at 0.10 -- unverified but not contradicted, since there are zero real matches either way. Full-corpus diff (before vs after, all 12,600 rows, computed not assumed): exactly 89 rows changed, all from KXLOVEISLANDUSARANK-26AUG31RTOP3, and all landed correctly on the existing 'competition/award ranking' many-way-field rule via the title's own 'season 8' phrasing (not left unmatched) -- a strictly better classification, not just a removal. Zero unintended regressions anywhere else in the corpus.
items.notes: 2 new tests in tests/test_scanner.py: test_political_coup_couples_misfire_fixed (confirms the misfire is gone and the title now lands on 'competition/award ranking'), test_political_coup_genuine_phrasing_still_matches (confirms genuine coup phrasing still gets 0.10/'political coup' after padding). Full suite green (2412 passed, 1 skipped, 13 subtests passed).

items.title: 'NASA mission' heuristic misfires on LPGA golfer names ('Wannasaen', 'Nasa Hataoka') -- one collision fixed, one flagged as structurally unfixable
items.action: Found via a systematic sweep of core.scanner._HEURISTIC_RULES, not reactively -- every prior heuristic recalibration (win-catchall, sports-award, hurricane, down-ballot-election, win-catchall-two-team-game-misfire) was found because someone happened to notice a specific bug. This pass instead ran analysis/heuristic_backtest.py fresh against the full 12,600-row settled_markets corpus, then extracted every bare (unpadded, no internal space) keyword <=7 chars across all ~100 rules (55 candidates) and, for each, searched the full corpus for any OTHER real word containing it as a substring -- the exact mechanism this bug class needs. Bare 'nasa' (NASA mission rule, rate 0.30) is a substring of 'Wannasaen' (LPGA golfer Chanettee Wannasaen's surname) AND matches the standalone word 'Nasa' (LPGA golfer Nasa Hataoka's given name) -- confirmed against the full corpus: ALL 6 historical "NASA mission" matches (100%) traced to one ticker family, the ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open leaderboard ("Will [golfer] lead at the end of Round N...?"), zero real NASA-agency markets. These are two structurally different bugs: 'Wannasaen' is a mid-word substring collision (the same class as 'coup'/Couples and 'adcom'/Broadcom, fixable by space-padding), but 'Nasa Hataoka' is a genuine homograph -- her given name IS the standalone lowercased word "nasa", identical to the acronym, so even a strict word-boundary check (\bnasa\b) still matches it (verified: 3 of the 6 rows survive a boundary check). Padded the keyword to ' nasa ' (same fix pattern as ' coup '/' adcom ' above), which removes the Wannasaen collision (3 of 6 rows) but deliberately NOT the Hataoka one -- fixing that would require a name-specific blocklist (fragile, over-fit to one golfer) or matching on original casing/context this codebase's lowercased-substring architecture doesn't preserve; flagged as a known, structurally-unfixable residual rather than papered over with a hack. Rate left unchanged at 0.30 -- zero real NASA-agency matches either way; 'artemis'/'moon landing'/etc. in the same rule remain the reliable path to a real match (verified the existing parametrized test for "Will NASA's Artemis mission launch..." still resolves correctly via 'artemis', independent of the 'nasa' padding). Full-corpus diff (before vs after, all 12,600 rows): exactly 3 rows changed (the Wannasaen rows, 0.30/'NASA mission' -> unmatched/None); the 3 Hataoka rows are unchanged by design, still misfiring. Zero unintended regressions elsewhere.

items.title: daily_smart_money.py committed the whole git index, not just its own data file -- fixed
items.action: Found 2026-09-08 while investigating a real incident: a dashboard-ux agent had git-add-staged its own in-progress files (core/logger.py, dashboard/pages/4_Smart_Money.py, tests/test_smart_money_fills.py) before a session-limit interruption, then the autonomous scripts/daily_smart_money.py scheduled task ran under the same git identity and silently folded those already-staged files into its own generic "data: smart money scan 2026-09-08..." commit (3fd8223) -- nothing was lost (git log --oneline -- <path> found it), but it looked identical to lost work from git status/git diff alone. Root cause: the script correctly scoped its own git-add call to just its one intended data file, but its final git-commit call (no pathspec) commits the ENTIRE index, not just what the script itself staged -- a bare commit always commits everything staged, regardless of who staged it. The preceding cached-diff no-changes check was also unscoped, so it would not have caught or warned about this either.
items.notes: Fixed both spots in scripts/daily_smart_money.py: the no-changes check is now scoped to the one data-file path this script owns (git diff --cached --name-only -- <path>), and the commit is now git's pathspec-scoped commit form (git commit -m msg -- <path>) -- commits only that path's staged changes, leaves anything else already staged in the index untouched for its actual owner to commit separately. No test harness added, consistent with this project's existing precedent for direct-subprocess/git orchestration scripts (main.py, daily_resolve_first.py) having no pytest coverage by design -- verified via ast.parse syntax check instead. Documented from the dashboard-ux agent side too: see .claude/agents/leviathan-dashboard-ux.md's 2026-09-07 'staged-but-uncommitted change can get swept into an unrelated automated commit' lesson for the incident narrative this fix addresses the root cause of.

items.title: Dynamic sizing turned on at $50+confidence scaling; fixed a real bug where headline P&L was never actually dollar-scaled
items.action: User request 2026-09-08: raise unit_size 10->50, keep the existing confidence_stake_multipliers (HIGH 1.5 / MED 1.0 / LOW 0.5), turn dynamic_sizing_enabled on (the live-metrics half of its gate -- resolved_count>=30 AND resolved_count_per_category_max>=15 -- had already cleared at 38/16), and apply the new sizing to past resolved bets too, not just future ones. While implementing, found a real, separate, pre-existing bug: core.logger.get_stats()'s total_hypothetical_pnl -- the figure every display site (daily plaintext report, weekly plaintext digest, weekly HTML digest, analysis/calibration.py) labeled as dollars -- was actually the raw SUM(pnl_if_traded), a per-$1-notional ratio, never multiplied by unit_size OR stake_size_hypothetical at all. This meant every 'Hypothetical P&L' figure ever shown in a live email was silently ~unit_size times too low (e.g. a true $12.39 at the old $10 flat unit displayed as $1.24), identical regardless of what unit_size was configured. Fixed as part of this same change since leaving it unfixed would have made the new $50+confidence sizing invisible in every report -- the headline number would not have moved at all.
items.notes: core/logger.py: added backfill_stake_sizes(config) -- recomputes stake_size_hypothetical for every already-resolved paper signal via core.sizing.compute_stake_size(), the exact function resolve_outcomes() already uses, so backfilled and freshly-resolved rows are computed identically. Also fixed get_stats()'s SQL: total_hypothetical_pnl is now SUM(pnl_if_traded * COALESCE(stake_size_hypothetical, 10.0)) -- real dollars, with legacy pre-column rows falling back to $10 (the actual historical flat unit_size in effect when they resolved, not the current live unit_size, so old rows aren't retroactively re-priced at a stake they were never sized at). core/report.py: removed the now-misleading '($10/contract)' label on the daily plaintext Track Record line (the figure is a blended stake-weighted total now, not a flat per-unit figure). analysis/calibration.py: its headline print no longer re-multiplies get_stats()'s already-dollar value by unit_size (was about to double-scale). config.json / config.example.json: unit_size 10->50, dynamic_sizing_enabled true->on. Ran backfill live: 370 resolved paper signals updated (includes PASS rows, matching resolve_outcomes()'s own unfiltered scope -- harmless, PASS always has pnl_if_traded=0). Real result: the 38 non-PASS resolved signals' total_hypothetical_pnl moved from the old buggy $1.24-equivalent display to a correct $64.50 at the new $50+confidence sizing (vs. ~$61.95 if every row had been MED/1.0x at flat $50 -- the 2 HIGH and 2 LOW confidence rows pulled the weighted total slightly above that baseline). 10 new/updated tests in tests/test_logger.py (get_stats dollar-weighting, legacy-NULL fallback, backfill_stake_sizes: updates resolved rows, skips unresolved rows, ignores real_fill rows, overwrites stale flat values). Full suite green. NOT fixed, deliberately scoped out: ~12 other core.logger.get_stats_by_*() breakdown functions (get_stats_by_sig/flag_path/confidence/heuristic_label/etc.) have the identical raw-ratio display bug in their own total_pnl fields, consumed by report.py's per-group tables and analysis/calibration.py's _pnl() helper -- left untouched given the size of a full sweep; see the sibling item this note points future work to.

items.action: PM workflow audit (2026-09-08, user asked what else could be automated/streamlined): plain json.load() applies Python's last-key-wins rule on a duplicate object key with no error and no warning. items.title: Fixed a structural win/loss measurement bug in smart-money tracking; found one genuine winner (Poligarch) via a corrected broad scan
items.action: User (2026-09-08): 'So I want to take a look at the winning traders and whale portion... How are we tracking winning traders, do traders with a high win % worth tailing bets using a paper fill etc please do extensive research and come to a determination and create a plan of attack.' Investigation found Polymarket's Data API /positions currentValue/curPrice/percentPnl/cashPnl fields read ~0/~-100% for EVERY resolved position regardless of actual win/loss (confirmed across 1,479 resolved positions, 20 wallets) -- sources.accounts._score_wallet's win-rate math was structurally incapable of ever detecting a win.
items.notes: Fix: sources.accounts.fetch_market_resolution() cross-references Polymarket's CLOB API (/markets/{condition_id}, tokens[].winner) as independent ground truth, verified live against a real position and cross-checked against Gamma's outcomePrices. fetch_resolutions_for_positions() caches resolutions permanently on disk (immutable once a market settles). _score_wallet() rewritten to compute true win/loss and true $ P&L (realizedPnl + payout-if-won - initialValue) instead of the broken fields; gate_checklist() and get_wallet_profile() added for the new Trader Profile dashboard page (dashboard/pages/6_Trader_Profile.py) -- plain-language pass/fail per gate, current bets, full resolved bet history. FINDING 1: re-verified all 20 config.json watchlist wallets (curated by monthly $-PnL leaderboard rank) with the fix -- 0/20 show any real win on a position held to resolution. wan123 alone: 227 verified positions, 0 wins, -$1.88M. Confirms these wallets are profitable TRADERS (exiting before resolution), not skilled FORECASTERS -- $-PnL rank and resolution accuracy are different populations. This watchlist is not a valid source for tailing. FINDING 2: ran discover_winners() over a broad, differently-sourced live sample (1000 recent trades -> 457 unique wallets, NOT the $-PnL leaderboard) to test whether real winners exist anywhere. Exactly ONE wallet passed every _is_winner() gate: Poligarch (0xb40e89677d59665d5188541ad860450a6e2a7cc9) -- 64.5% win rate on 397 resolved bets (live-reverified), +$11,233 real P&L. Statistically strong (SE ~2.4% at this n, well clear of both the 50% coin-flip line and the 55% gate), not a fluke of a thin sample. Added to config.json's watchlist so the existing fill-tracking pipeline (Panel 4, core.logger.record_smart_money_fills) starts recording their real bets as paper fills going forward -- verified end-to-end (fetch_watchlist_positions() correctly returns them). This is passive tracking only, NOT active tailing -- Leviathan does not yet place its own paper bets mirroring Poligarch's. PM read: hold off on building that until Poligarch's edge is validated prospectively (a few more weeks of live observation) rather than committing engineering effort to a sample of one. OPERATIONAL FIX (found while reasoning through next steps): the broad scan took ~19 hours end-to-end this session (fighting repeated, unpredictable background-job kills in this environment, worked around via aggressive per-wallet checkpointing). More importantly: discover_winners() is called synchronously from main.py's daily pipeline (enrich_with_smart_money -> load_winners) whenever the 24h winner cache goes stale, but main.py's own scheduled task has only a 10-minute ExecutionTimeLimit -- per-wallet cost is highly variable and unbounded by discovery_sample_size alone (a single large wallet's live resolution fetches can take many minutes), so without a fix, the NEXT time the cache went stale, main.py's daily run would very likely have blown through its time limit and been killed -- silently breaking the entire daily pipeline, not just smart money. Fixed via a new config key accounts.discovery_time_budget_s (default 120s, deliberately small relative to main.py's 10-min ceiling): discover_winners() now stops checking new wallets once the wall-clock budget is hit and returns whatever winners were found among wallets actually reached, rather than risking an unbounded hang. The permanent on-disk resolution cache means later runs cover more ground for the same budget as it warms up. Test suite: 2384 passed (was 2366 at session start; +18 net across the true-resolution fix, gate_checklist/get_wallet_profile, fetch_new=False cache-only mode, and the time-budget behavior).
